thread:
lina: Quick follow-up thread from today's all-hands focused on pricing/packaging/usage policy. Drop short clarifying Qs and we'll route.
sam: Two quick ones: 1) if a customer is actively using credits but hits the 12mo expiry, can we auto-extend or prorate? 2) can credits be applied to invoices (e.g., marketplace or seat charges) or only API usage?
julia: Legal/Finance: default credits expire 12 months from issue and do not auto-renew. For strategic customers we can consider manual extensions or top-ups (requires approval). By default credits apply to API usage only; exceptions must be explicitly included in promos. We'll publish examples in the FAQ.
maya: Rate/quotas question: do we have route-level quotas (tokens per route) vs project-wide quotas? Some customers want per-endpoint throttles to protect expensive paths.
ethan: Yes we support per-route soft quotas and project-level hard quotas. Defaults are conservative: project default token quota ~5,000,000 tokens/day and route soft quotas are often set by DevEx/CSM per account. Soft quotas queue briefly and emit metrics; hard quotas return 429.
tim: Sales note: for Dedicated, burst pools are prepaid and can be allocated to particular routes in the contract (helps high-cost endpoints). Billing treats burst minutes separately from committed capacity.
ops-bot: info: created ORG-940 to track per-route quota templates and admin UI for allocating burst pools to routes.
sam: Can multiple projects pool credits or quotas under a single org? Some platform teams asked about transferring unused quota between projects.
julia: We don't allow automatic transfer of credits between distinct billing accounts. For enterprise orgs we can do org-level pools (single invoice, pooled quota) under an agreed contract. Individual free/trial credits remain tied to the issuing account.
maya: On headers: any plans to expose ETA if requests are queued? That helps customer UX.
ethan: We're experimenting with an experimental header `X-Queue-ETA-ms` in canary; it may be noisy but could help. Currently GA headers are `X-RateLimit-Limit`, `X-RateLimit-Remaining`, and `X-RateLimit-Reset`. ETA header is opt-in behind a flag while we measure accuracy.
devex: I'll produce a concise "Rate & Quota playbook" for CSM/Sales with sample cURL snippets parsing headers, recommended soft quota numbers, and an escalation checklist (when to recommend Dedicated, Optimize, or a burst pool). Draft by Wednesday.
lina: Action items: 1) @devex one-pager on quotas/headers/playbook 2) @julia update billing FAQ with extension/top-up flow examples 3) eng-runtime to review ORG-940 (per-route quotas & burst assignment). I'll post the compiled follow-up doc to #docs once we have drafts.
sam: thanks. small ask: can finance provide an email template for customers requesting credit extensions (to speed approvals)?
julia: We'll draft a template and attach approval criteria.
maya: thanks all 44b
lina: Closing loop for now; add anything else here and I'll fold into the follow-up doc.
